title: T2DM with chronic systolic CHF and in-office EKG
encounterNote: 58-year-old male presenting for routine follow-up of type 2 diabetes mellitus and chronic systolic heart failure. Patient reports mild shortness of breath on exertion, but no acute chest pain. Current medications: metformin 1000 mg twice daily and lisinopril 20 mg daily. Examination shows mild lower extremity edema; lungs are clear to auscultation. Assessed as stable chronic T2DM without complications and stable chronic systolic heart failure. A 12-lead EKG was performed in the office today; it showed normal sinus rhythm without acute ischemic changes. Continue current medications and follow up in three months.
